title: Vault profile rename orphans live secrets in Windows Credential Manager forever
existing_state: When a vault profile is renamed, PersistVaultProfileByIndex updates the list display and default-profile tracking (SettingsDialog.cs:997-1005) and then re-saves the four secrets under the NEW name (1011-1017) — but never deletes the old ssh_helper:vault:<oldname>:* targets. The notifications tab does this correctly via MigrateNotificationCredential, which copies then deletes the old target (1584-1593); the vault tab has no equivalent. Every rename therefore leaves a complete, working copy of the vault token / AppRole secret-id / LDAP password / userpass password under the stale name in Windows Credential Manager, readable by any process running as the user, with no UI that will ever list or clean it up (BtnVaultRemove_Click at 851-858 only deletes targets for names currently in the profile list).
recommendation: In PersistVaultProfileByIndex's rename branch (after line 997's name-change check), migrate the four credentials the same way notifications do: read old target, save under new target, DeletePassword the old one. Extract MigrateNotificationCredential into a shared helper taking the target-builder Func and reuse it for the four VaultAuthTarget types.
user_benefit: Stops live vault tokens and directory passwords from silently accumulating under dead names in the OS credential store every time a profile is renamed.

evidence.note: Rename branch updates display only; secrets re-saved under new name, old targets untouched
Notifications already implement the correct migrate+delete pattern — vault drifted from it
